column1: # English-French glossary of the aXqua documentation.
# docs/i18n/translate.py puts the French term into the English sentence before the sentence is
# translated, in title case ("The Courbe De Tarage at the Frontière De Sortie"): the engine copies a
# capitalized term like a name, chooses the article and the agreement itself ("La courbe de tarage
# ... est synthétisée"), and the case is restored afterwards. Sent in lower case, rare French words
# are translated a second time ("courbe de tarage" came back as "courbe de goudron"). A longer term
# wins over a shorter one inside it. An acronym (all capitals) matches in capitals only. The gender
# (m or f) makes the articles in front of the term agree ("un tâche" -> "une tâche").
# Reference for terms: https://www.termdat.bk.admin.ch/ and the French manuals of TELEMAC.
